title: Uniform mass of each Boolean input
statement:
Let $n$ be a natural number, and regard the type of $n$-bit Boolean inputs $\mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \mathrm{Bool}$ as a finite probability space, with its associated probability mass function $p$. Then for every input $x$, the mass assigned to $x$, viewed as a real number, is
\[
p(x) = \frac{1}{2^{\,n}}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: PMF taken from the finite probability space structure on the Boolean inputs
replaced:
Every element $x : \mathrm{BoolInput}\,n$ has PMF weight $2^{-n}$ under the uniform
distribution: $\mathrm{toPMF}(\mathrm{BoolInput}\,n,\, x) = 2^{-n}$.
